summary: Granite Mountain's 20-foot steel tower dates to 1962 per Canada Lookouts; towermen lists tie staff to Granite until 2001, and no source describes the site today.

events.note: Canada Lookouts says the smokejumpers erected a new 20-foot steel tower at Granite Mountain in 1962, citing a Department of Natural Resources annual report for 1962-63.
Towermen list says Basil Natamogen was full time on the Granite and Petitte towers in 1968; the entry does not clearly separate the two.
Towermen list says he went back to Granite until 2001; the same entry does not clearly separate Granite Mountain from Petitte Granite.

notes_for_editor: The 1962 build year, 20 ft height and steel construction come from one Canada Lookouts line that cites a DNR annual report for 1962-63. The word 'new' implies an earlier structure at this site, but no source read describes one, so none is recorded. The Basil Natamogen entry names 'Granite' and 'Petitte Granite (40')' without clearly separating the two; the 1968 and 2001 events and the staffing as_of rest on reading 'Granite' as Granite Mountain. The 'all towers condemned' line does not name Granite Mountain and is used only as a caveat. Staffing status is unknown with as_of 2001, the last year the entry gives for Granite. The websiteservice listing gives no height, so the 6.1 m figure comes from the Canada Lookouts line only. A Forestry Chronicle article on the Saskatchewan smokejumpers (search hit) could not be fetched (403) and is not used. Access, current status and site condition: no source found. Searches used: 2. Agency removed: no source names the operator; the Department of Natural Resources appears only as the annual report that Canada Lookouts cites. The listing's GRANITE row has no height, year or notes; the 105' height and 1954 cupola on that page belong to another row.
